task.description:
Design a fix for the ISS-0113/ISS-0423-disclosed remaining hazard that ISS-0480 caught recurring in the wild: `Letflow.TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1`'s unconditional `Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)` call (test/support/tenant_fixture.ex:222) is a GLOBAL per-repo setting, so any one of the 44 still-unconverted call sites running mid-suite forcibly checks in EVERY other concurrently-running async test's connection -- including tests that never call provisioned_tenant!/1 themselves and have no way to defend against it. Read this run's ISSUE-FIXER diagnosis (handoffs/WF03-ISS0480-20260905/step-0.5-1-issue-fixer-diagnose.json result.summary) in full first -- it traces the mechanism through Ecto's own sandbox.ex source (mode/2's documented 'checks in connections being used in any other test running concurrently' behaviour) and captured three live, real occurrences across two full-suite runs, each against a different victim test. This is not a fresh investigation; treat the mechanism as established fact.

This is NOT a new root cause -- it is ISS-0113/ISS-0423's own explicitly disclosed remaining scope (44 of 46 TenantFixture call sites unconverted) actually manifesting. Read docs/issues/ISS-0113.yaml's full resolution_note and docs/issues/ISS-0423.yaml's full resolution_note before designing -- both already contain load-bearing prior art you must not silently re-attempt:
  - ISS-0113's FIRST attempted fix (an opts[:restore_sandbox] opt-in doing Sandbox.mode(:manual) + a fresh checkout after provisioning) was tried for real, passed its own design gate, then FAILED at implementation (26/38) -- traced to a 4th Sandbox.mode/2 mechanism: Ecto's Sandbox.mode/2 checks in ALL pool connections whenever the requested mode differs from the pool's CURRENT one, so a second mid-test mode flip (the restore step itself) discards the connection provisioning had just populated. Do not propose a per-call restore-to-:manual step without addressing this exact failure mode head-on.
  - The mechanism that DID work for the 2 already-converted files (secrets_test.exs, webhooks_test.exs) is: no restore at all, relying on the pre-existing unconditional :auto call being 'ALREADY SUFFICIENT... PROVIDED the call site is independently verified' against three (now four, per ISS-0423's own resolution note) named failure mechanisms (self-checkout, concurrent multi-process DB access, second provisioning call, and this run's own newly-confirmed global-blast-radius-on-OTHER-files mechanism). That per-call-site verification approach is exactly what leaves 44 sites (and therefore every OTHER async: true test in the suite, including files with NO TenantFixture involvement at all, like ISS-0480's own two victims) permanently exposed until every site is converted or defended -- which is why ISS-0480 recurred.

YOUR DESIGN MUST DECIDE, and justify the choice with reasoning grounded in the diagnosis (not merely restate the options): 
(a) NARROW: continue the per-call-site conversion tranche approach (verify + flip async:false->true one file at a time against the four named mechanisms) for some or all of the remaining 44 TenantFixture call sites. This does NOT close the hazard for the two ISS-0480 victim files themselves (they already ARE async: true and call NO fixture) -- it only reduces how often the global mode-flip fires, proportional to how many of the 44 you convert. State plainly whether a partial narrow conversion actually protects RowApprovalTest/PackUpdateMigrationTest, or whether ONLY converting all 44 (or another structural change) removes their exposure. 
(b) STRUCTURAL: remove the global-blast-radius hazard at its source, so files with NO TenantFixture involvement (like ISS-0480's own two victims) stop being exposed regardless of how many of the 44 remaining call sites are converted or not. Concrete directions worth evaluating (not prescriptive -- you decide, but show your reasoning against each): a separate, dedicated Ecto.Repo/connection pool for TenantFixture-provisioned tenant schemas so its Sandbox.mode/2 flips never touch Letflow.Repo's pool that ordinary DataCase tests use; or moving provisioned_tenant!/1's schema provisioning off the sandboxed Repo pool entirely (e.g. a raw, non-sandboxed connection dedicated to migration replay, never touching Sandbox.mode/2 on the shared pool at all); or something else you identify as removing the mode/2 call's global reach. Check each candidate against decision 0009-test-parallel-pool-sizing.md's DBConnection budget arithmetic (a second pool/connection changes peak concurrent connection demand) and against Letflow.SandboxPool's own existing moduledoc (test/support -- there is already a quota-bounded, owner-monitored pool abstraction in this codebase built for exactly this shape; evaluate whether it's reusable here or whether TenantFixture's needs are different enough to warrant its own mechanism).

Whichever direction you choose, or if you choose a hybrid, your design's normative section must be unambiguous enough for ELIXIR-DEV to implement without further judgement calls, per this project's weak-model-tolerance standard. State explicitly: what changes, what does NOT change (public API of provisioned_tenant!/1, error taxonomy, any existing call site's return shape), and what verification ELIXIR-DEV/TEST-DESIGNER must run to prove the fix actually closes ISS-0480's specific exposure (RowApprovalTest and PackUpdateMigrationTest must stop being vulnerable to ANY concurrently-running TenantFixture-using test, not merely stop failing in one lucky run -- a fail-then-pass regression test per WF-03 Step 4 must be able to demonstrate this, so your design should suggest how such a test could deterministically trigger the hazard pre-fix, e.g. by forcing a concurrent provisioned_tenant!/1 call while a DataCase-only test holds an in-flight transaction, mirroring ISS-0110's own targeted-reproduction technique of simulating the race directly rather than relying on suite-wide timing luck).

Do not touch supervision-tree files. Do not write implementation code -- design artefact only, in lib/letflow/design/, per this project's design/implementation split.

REWORK ITERATION 1: ELIXIR-DEV implemented design section 10.3 exactly as specified and it works correctly for the core mechanism (172 tests passed across the actual ISS-0480 victims -- test/letflow/row_approval_test.exs, test/letflow/definitions/pack_update_migration_test.exs -- the 2 already-async files, and 9 more TenantFixture-calling files; zero unexpected failures; OQ-6's ISS-0110/TenantSchemaReaper tag-interaction check confirmed safe against real source). BUT section 10.4's claim 'every existing call site's own source... requires zero edits to keep working exactly as before' is FALSE for 2 of the 46 call sites, confirmed by real execution with a git-stash baseline comparison (not implementer error -- CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's static read could not have caught this; only running the code surfaced it):

1. test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_test.exs -- 8/14 pass (was 14/14 on the unmodified tree). Its own `hard_cleanup/1` helper (lines 426-434), called from an `on_exit(fn -> hard_cleanup(fixture.tenant_id) end)` at line 422, does a bare `Repo.query!(DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS ... CASCADE)` against Letflow.Repo directly from the on_exit process (not a descendant of the test process, no ambient checkout) -- this depended on Letflow.Repo already being in :auto mode as a side effect of provisioned_tenant!/1's OLD behavior, which your fix correctly removes. Now fails: `** (EXIT) shutdown: "owner ... exited"`.

2. test/letflow/definitions/promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs -- 3/12 pass (was 12/12 on the unmodified tree). Its own local helpers (`drop_schema!` line 100-101, `schema_exists?`/`sandbox_process_definition_ids` lines 144-157) all call bare `Repo.query!` against Letflow.Repo directly, and its own moduledoc explicitly documents relying on provisioned_tenant!/1's 'same sandbox :auto switch' side effect for a SECOND real provisioning call within the same test body (this is mechanism (c) from ISS-0113's own three named failure mechanisms, restated in design section 2). One failure changes an expected error tuple shape because the second provisioning call now hits a connection in :manual mode instead of :auto.

YOUR REWORK TASK: decide and specify, in a new subsection under section 10 (e.g. 10.8), how these 2 files are handled -- WITHOUT reopening or weakening section 10.3's core mechanism, which is proven correct and must not change. You have two directions to choose between (or another you identify), same as your original design task's own decision-and-justify standard:
(a) Declare these 2 files' own local helpers in-scope for a narrow, explicit edit -- e.g. their on_exit/helper functions call Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo, :auto) + Ecto.Repo.put_dynamic_repo(Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo) themselves before their own bare Repo calls, mirroring the same seam provisioned_tenant!/1 itself now uses internally -- state precisely what each of the 2 files' helpers must call, so ELIXIR-DEV does not have to invent the fix.
(b) Some other compatibility mechanism you identify -- but explicitly reject any approach that would restore Letflow.Repo's pool to :auto mode as a general side effect again, since that reintroduces the exact ISS-0480 hazard this fix exists to remove. State why any such approach avoids that trap if you propose one.

Either way, revise section 10.4's 'zero call-site edits' claim explicitly to state the true, narrowed scope (44 of 46 need zero edits; these 2 need a stated, specific edit) rather than leaving the false blanket claim standing. Full detail: handoffs/WF03-ISS0480-20260905/step-03a-elixir-dev.json result.summary and result.issues[0].
acceptance_criteria: Design artefact written to lib/letflow/design/ (a new file, or a new section appended to lib/letflow/design/iss0113-tenant-fixture-sandbox-restore-opt-in.md if you judge it the same design lineage -- your call, state which and why)

Explicitly addresses whether a narrow per-call-site conversion tranche can ever fully protect a file with zero TenantFixture involvement (like ISS-0480's two victims), or whether only a structural fix does -- this determines whether ISS-0480 can be marked resolved by this fix or only instrumented
Does not re-propose the exact restore_sandbox mechanism ISS-0113 already tried and reverted, without explaining what is different this time if some variant of it is chosen
States precisely what changes and what does not (public API, error taxonomy, existing call sites' behavior)
Reconciles against decision 0009-test-parallel-pool-sizing.md's DBConnection budget arithmetic if the design adds any connection/pool

Describes a concrete, deterministic mechanism TEST-DESIGNER can use to construct a fail-then-pass regression test for ISS-0480's specific exposure (a forced concurrent TenantFixture call racing a plain DataCase test), not merely 'run the suite many times and hope it reproduces'
No implementation code in the design artefact (design signatures/@specs/data-flow only)

result.summary:
REWORK ITERATION 1 (this result): closes the single BLOCKER ELIXIR-DEV's real-execution scoped test run found in the otherwise-proven-correct §10 structural fix -- design section 10.8 added to lib/letflow/design/iss0113-tenant-fixture-sandbox-restore-opt-in.md, §10.4's 'zero call-site edits' claim revised to state its true, narrowed scope (44 of 46 need zero edits; 2 named files need a small, specific edit to their OWN local helpers, precisely stated in §10.8 rather than left as a false blanket claim). §10.0-10.7 (the core ProvisioningRepo/put_dynamic_repo mechanism) are UNCHANGED and NOT reopened -- ELIXIR-DEV's own 172-test scoped run already proved that mechanism correct, including both actual ISS-0480 victims (RowApprovalTest, PackUpdateMigrationTest).

ROOT CAUSE, re-verified by direct read of both files (not inherited from the rework handoff's own description): both failing files have their own hand-rolled helpers that call bare Repo (= Letflow.Repo, via DataCase's `alias Letflow.Repo`) directly, bypassing TenantFixture's public API/teardown boundary entirely, and each depended on provisioned_tenant!/1's now-correctly-removed side effect of leaving Letflow.Repo in :auto mode for the rest of the calling test.

1. test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_test.exs: broken_state_tenant!/1 (line 421) calls provisioned_tenant!/1 with teardown: false and registers its OWN on_exit(fn -> hard_cleanup(fixture.tenant_id) end) instead. hard_cleanup/1 (lines 426-434) issues the same 3 statements TenantFixture's own teardown/2 issues (DROP SCHEMA, 2x Repo.delete_all), directly against Letflow.Repo, from an on_exit process with no ambient checkout -- this needed Letflow.Repo already in :auto mode, which no longer happens post-fix.
2. test/letflow/definitions/promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs: NOT its 3 bare-Repo helpers (drop_schema!/1, schema_exists?/1, sandbox_process_definition_ids/1) -- those operate on SandboxPool-provisioned sandbox schemas (a distinct mechanism from TenantFixture, confirmed unaffected: SandboxPool's own DB worker still calls Letflow.Repo directly per already-shipped §10.1, unchanged by this rework). The actual regression is the AC1 test's own REAL second SandboxPool.claim/2 call (line 462, exhausting a dedicated pool) needing a real :auto-mode window on Letflow.Repo to run its own migrator work in -- a window the pre-fix code got for free, as an unintended side effect, from provisioned_tenant/0's earlier call in the same test.

DIRECTION CHOSEN: (a) -- both files' own helpers/wrappers call the SAME seam TenantFixture itself now uses internally (Ecto.Repo.put_dynamic_repo/1 + Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.mode/2 targeting Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo), rather than any mechanism that would restore Letflow.Repo's pool to :auto mode as a GENERAL/ambient side effect (explicitly rejected, per the handoff's own instruction, since that would reintroduce ISS-0480's exact hazard):
- File 1 (§10.8.2.1): hard_cleanup/1 wraps its 3 existing Repo calls in Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo, :auto) + Repo.put_dynamic_repo(Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo)/restore-in-after -- mirroring with_provisioning_repo/1's own already-shipped shape exactly. No change to broken_state_tenant!/1's own provisioned_tenant!/1 call, drop_table!/2, table_exists?/2, or any test-body-run helper (only the on_exit-run hard_cleanup/1, which has no ambient checkout, needs this).
- File 2 (§10.8.2.2): NOT the 3 SandboxPool-facing helpers (correctly left untouched -- wrapping them would fix nothing, since they were never routed through TenantFixture/ProvisioningRepo). provisioned_tenant/0 (this file's own thin wrapper around TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1) gains ONE new leading statement, Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto), made once, by this file itself -- safe because this file is async: false (confirmed, unchanged), so ExUnit never schedules it concurrently with any async: true file; this is exactly the same kind of call §9.3/§9.4 already established as safe for a non-concurrent caller, not a reopening of Mechanism 4 (§9.2) since no restore-to-:manual step is added (that mid-test restore is what made Mechanism 4 fail, not the initial :auto call itself). No Repo.put_dynamic_repo/1 needed here since the target is Letflow.Repo itself, not ProvisioningRepo -- SandboxPool's migrator work runs on Letflow.Repo directly, per §10.1.

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE (§10.8.3, stated explicitly): test/support/tenant_fixture.ex and test/support/provisioning_repo.ex are untouched by this rework -- neither file's edit modifies TenantFixture's public API, with_provisioning_repo/1, or ProvisioningRepo. §10.4's claim for the other 44 files is unaffected. Letflow.Repo's pool-wide :auto mode is NOT restored as a GENERAL side effect anywhere -- the one new Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) call added is scoped to exactly one async: false file's own test-support code, for a reason unrelated to TenantFixture, and cannot reach any async: true test (the ISS-0480 hazard's own precondition). No test assertion text changes in either file -- both edits are additions inside existing private helper functions' own bodies. No new file, module, or config.

Verification ELIXIR-DEV must run (§10.8.4, given to close this rework): (1) tenant_fixture_test.exs back to 14/14 (pre-§10 baseline), (2) promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs back to 12/12 (pre-§10 baseline), with particular attention to AC1's exact assertions passing for the right reason, (3) re-run the original 172-test §10 scoped set to confirm no new regression outside these 2 files, (4) mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force clean.

No implementation code written in the design artefact -- §10.8 states call ordering/seam usage in prose (design-level, not literal Elixir), matching this project's design/implementation split.
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR to re-gate the revised design (§10.4's corrected claim + new §10.8) before ELIXIR-DEV resumes implementation: verify §10.8.2.1's hard_cleanup/1 wrap (test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_test.exs) and §10.8.2.2's provisioned_tenant/0 leading Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) statement (test/letflow/definitions/promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs) are each precisely specified enough to implement without further judgement calls, that §10.8.3's 'does not reintroduce ISS-0480' reasoning holds, and that §10.0-10.7's core mechanism is genuinely untouched (no regression to what already passed 172/172). Then back to ELIXIR-DEV to apply exactly these 2 local edits and run §10.8.4's verification list (both files back to their pre-§10 baselines: 14/14 and 12/12; the original 172-test scoped set re-run clean; mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force clean).
